extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, disciplinary counsel, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal public reprimand under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state public reprimand; describes the grounds for discipline, the factual misconduct, and the procedural/publication steps the USPTO will take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline upon Respondent identical to the discipline imposed by the Commonwealth of Massachusetts Board of Bar Overseers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 must be sent to the respondent (here, by certified mail) informing the respondent of the request for reciprocal discipline and providing an opportunity to respond. The respondent may file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose reciprocal discipline identical to state discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State (i.e., the same form of discipline: public reprimand, suspension, disbarment, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice requested that the USPTO impose a reciprocal discipline identical to the Commonwealth's public reprimand. If the procedural and substantive conditions of § 11.24 are met (and no successful opposition is raised), the USPTO will order the identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: No genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination whether there is a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) governs whether reciprocal discipline may be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not oppose the imposition of reciprocal discipline on the statutory/regulatory grounds enumerated in § 11.24(d), the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and find that imposing reciprocal discipline is appropriate. In this case, Respondent's counsel stated Respondent 'does not challenge the propriety' and 'does not raise any issue of fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)-(iv),' leading to the determination that no genuine issue exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is publicly reprimanded for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order publicly reprimands the respondent under this regulatory provision, and notes the USPTO action is predicated upon the state public reprimand. (The Order itself does not elaborate on the full text of § 11.804(h) but cites it as the regulatory basis for discipline.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Massachusetts Rule 8.4(c): dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent's conduct was found to violate Rule 8.4(c) of the Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct: 'engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete factual example given: 'The Respondent notarized a fellow employee's wife's signature on two occasions when she was not present, had not signed the documents in his presence, and had not indicated that her signature was voluntarily affixed for the purposes stated within the document,' conduct characterized as dishonesty/fraud/misrepresentation under Rule 8.4(c). This factual predicate from the state proceeding is used to support the USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural notice, publication, and reporting requirements (Official Gazette and 37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish a Notice in the Official Gazette and to give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, to courts where the respondent is admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the text of the Notice of Public Reprimand for publication and requires dissemination to relevant disciplinary agencies and courts. It also references that disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of notice by certified mail and 40-day response period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt no. provided) notifying Respondent and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service (here, certified mail) and adherence to the 40-day response period are procedural prerequisites for the USPTO to consider reciprocal discipline under § 11.24. The Order illustrates that a timely response was filed (by counsel) and that failure to contest the grounds can lead to a finding of no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority for disciplinary action (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's authority to take this disciplinary action is pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions by the USPTO must cite and be taken under the appropriate statutory and regulatory provisions. The Order explicitly states the action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, anchoring the disciplinary power and procedures invoked.
